In 15 taraṅgas (See New Catalogus Catalogurum (NCC). Vols 1-36: vol. 12, p. 136a). The work deals with 15 subjects which either directly or indirectly relate to Advaita Vedānta: 1) purāṇaprāmāṇyavivekaḥ, 2) trivargatattvavivekaḥ, 3) mokṣatattvavivekaḥ, 4) caturvargasādhanavivekaḥ, 5) varṇāśramadharmāṇāṃ bhagavadārādhanarūpatvavivekaḥ, 6) varṇādidharmavivekaḥ, 7) bhagavadārādhanaviśeṣavivekaḥ, 8) nāmakīrtanādivivekaḥ, 9) bhagavadārādhanopapattivivekaḥ, 10) adhikārivivekaḥ, 11) tattvapadārthavivekaḥ, 12) vivekajñānaviṣayaikātmyavivekaḥ, 13) yogabahiraṅgavivekaḥ, 14) sayamaviṣayaphalavivekaḥ, 15) muktagativivekaḥ (See Descriptive Catalogue of Sanskrit Manuscripts in the Adyar Library (Adyar). Vols. 1–13: vol. 9, ms. 933).
Oppert I, ms. 3814, and Oppert II, mss. 3457, 7637, 9479, 9785, 9830. These 6 manuscripts are listed without the author's name.

Raṅganātha Sūri extols Kṛṣṇānanda Sarasvatī in a few verses at the beginning and end of the work. He includes biographical details about both himself and Kṛṣṇānanda Sarasvatī. See Raghavan, Venkataraman. Śāhendravilāsa of Śrīdhara Veṅkaṭeśa (A Poem on the Life of King Śāhaji of Tanjore, 1684-1710). Tiruchi: The Kalyan Press, 1952: p. 31.

This work is found in the name of Kṛṣṇānanda Sarasvatī in Bodhendra's Nāmāmṛtarasāyana. See Raghavan, Venkataraman. Śāhendravilāsa of Śrīdhara Veṅkaṭeśa (A Poem on the Life of King Śāhaji of Tanjore, 1684-1710). Tiruchi: The Kalyan Press, 1952: p. 31.
